read: partial: abstract, introduction, section 2 (contents, API, BIG-bench Lite, evaluation targets, human raters, canary string) and sections 3.1-3.2 (pp.1-12) in full; sections 3.3-6 (pp.12-26) skimmed; keyword table (p.47) and Appendix E on expert raters (p.48) read
venue_now: arXiv:2206.04615v3, 12 Jun 2023 (p.1); the acknowledgements thank 'the anonymous reviewers of TMLR' (p.42); no venue header in the text
what_it_is: BIG-bench (Beyond the Imitation Game) is a collaborative benchmark of 204 tasks contributed by 450 authors across 132 institutions, drawing on linguistics, childhood development, math, common-sense reasoning, biology, physics, social bias, software development and more, and chosen to be beyond the capabilities of current language models (p.2). About 80% of tasks are JSON tasks scored against targets by metrics such as exact string match, ROUGE or multiple-choice probabilities, and about 20% are programmatic Python tasks that can query the model over several rounds and use custom metrics (p.8). It evaluates OpenAI GPT-3 models and Google dense (BIG-G) and sparse transformers across orders of magnitude of scale, plus published PaLM results, against a team of expert human raters (p.2, pp.9-10).
domain: general: 204 language tasks across many fields; the task list in the text includes physics tasks but no engineering task (p.37)
size: 204 tasks (p.2); BIG-bench Lite subset of 24 JSON tasks (p.8); 109 multiple-choice JSON tasks (p.12); models: 13 BIG-G dense, BIG-G sparse, 8 GPT-3 sizes, PaLM (pp.9-10)
source_of_items: expert-written: tasks contributed by researchers through GitHub pull requests and peer-reviewed by discussion on the pull request (p.6)
instances: static: example lists for the JSON tasks (about 80%); the other 20% are programmatic tasks that interact with the model (p.8)
has_gold_traces: no: JSON tasks hold inputs and targets (p.8)
evaluation: mixed by task: exact string match, ROUGE and other generation metrics, multiple-choice grade, calibration (Brier score, ECE), and custom programmatic metrics; each task names one preferred metric, normalized to 0-100 for aggregates (p.8, p.11)
human_validation: Tasks were reviewed by discussion on GitHub pull requests (p.6). A team of expert raters performed the tasks to give mean and best human baselines, with internet access and sessions of 30 minutes to 2 hours; the paper warns these are lower bounds and that raters were not equally calibrated (p.10, p.48). No agreement statistics.
contamination_measures: a canary GUID string in every task file so that the data can be filtered out of training corpora, and a training_on_test_set task for post-hoc diagnosis (p.11); the evaluated models' training data predate the repository, so direct leakage is ruled out for them (pp.9-10)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-E1 (L182-190) names 'BIG-Bench' among 'Generalist suites ... [that] restrict assessment to factual recall via multiple-choice questions' but attributes it to Luo et al. (2024); this paper is not in the May reference list
engtrace_use.explanation: The characterization contradicts the paper. BIG-bench is not restricted to multiple choice: JSON tasks are scored by generation metrics such as exact string match and ROUGE as well as by multiple-choice probabilities, and about 20% of tasks are programmatic, multi-round tasks with custom metrics (p.8); 78 tasks carry the keyword 'free response' and 40 'programmatic' (p.47), against 109 multiple-choice JSON tasks (p.12). Nor is it a factual-recall test: tasks were selected to lie beyond current models (p.2), and 58 carry the keyword 'logical reasoning' and 23 'mathematics' (p.47). The task list shows no engineering task (p.37), so BIG-bench also gives little support to the sentence's subject, engineering evaluation.

suggested_wording: For the introduction's saturation and contamination point, not the engineering paragraph: 'BIG-bench (Srivastava et al., 2023) documents how quickly earlier benchmarks saturated and marks its 204 task files with a canary string so that they can be filtered out of training corpora.'
facts_to_cite: 204 tasks contributed by 450 authors across 132 institutions (p.2)
about 80% JSON tasks scored by metrics such as exact string match, ROUGE or multiple-choice grade; about 20% programmatic tasks that can query the model over multiple rounds (p.8)
expert human raters performed the tasks to provide a baseline (p.2, p.10)
a canary GUID string in every task file to keep BIG-bench out of training corpora (p.11)
'recent language-modeling benchmarks have often had short useful lifespans': superhuman SuperGLUE performance within 18 months (p.5; Figure 2, p.7)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: an explicit contamination measure (canary string, p.11), human expert baselines (p.10), and some code-defined tasks (programmatic tasks, p.8). Lacks: engineering content (none listed); generated parameterized instances with computed answers; gold intermediate traces; step-level evaluation; validation of an evaluator against experts.
notes: The May text names BIG-Bench but cites Luo et al. (2024), a text-to-image bias benchmark with a similar name. If the name stays, cite this paper (year per its TMLR version; the file is arXiv v3, 12 Jun 2023) and describe it accurately; it does not support S-E1's claim and is better used, if at all, in the introduction.
